extracted.intended_audience: American citizens (People of the State of New York) engaged in the 1787 ratification debate
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and evaluate defects in the Articles of Confederation and the necessary powers/features a national government must possess to preserve union, public safety, and justice. The text argues by historical example for constitutional remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional sanction / enforcement power
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States, as now composed, have no powers to exact obedience, or punish disobedience to their resolutions... There is no express delegation of authority to them to use force against delinquent members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national government must have an express power to enforce its laws (by pecuniary mulcts, suspension/divestiture of privileges, or other constitutional modes). Without such a sanction, the Confederacy exhibits a government 'destitute even of the shadow of constitutional power' to enforce its laws, risking dissolution or the usurpation of emergency powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual guaranty of State governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The want of a mutual guaranty of the State governments is another capital imperfection in the federal plan. There is nothing of this kind declared in the articles...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Union should be authorized to guaranty State constitutions against domestic violence or usurpation; such guaranty would not impede lawful, peaceful reform by a state's people but would permit federal assistance against violent overthrow, usurpation, tyranny, or faction-driven disorders (illustrated by Massachusetts' recent convulsions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on quotas for contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle of regulating the contributions of the States to the common treasury by QUOTAS is another fundamental error in the Confederation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotas fail as an equitable or practical measure of ability to pay (land value or population are poor proxies for wealth). Quotas produce glaring inequality and oppression, and are impracticable for raising adequate national revenues—historical confederacies waived quotas in practice or enforced them by force.

rubrics_metrics.name: National authority to raise its own revenues (imposts/excises)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no method of steering clear of this inconvenience, but by authorizing the national government to raise its own revenues in its own way. Imposts, excises, and, in general, all duties upon articles of consumption...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A federal government should be empowered to levy indirect taxes (imposts and excises) which 'find their level' and self-limit (too-high duties reduce consumption and revenue). Indirect taxes will likely form the chief part of early national revenue and avoid the inequalities of quota-based requisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer indirect taxes; use direct taxes only with practicable apportionment
rubrics_metrics.description: Impositions of this kind usually fall under the denomination of indirect taxes... Those of the direct kind, which principally relate to land and buildings, may admit of a rule of apportionment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect taxes are naturally limited and less oppressive; direct taxes (land/buildings) require an apportionment rule—population (numbers) is preferred over land valuation because valuations are costly and impracticable in a growing country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to regulate commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: The want of a power to regulate commerce is by all parties allowed to be of the number. ... there is no object that more strongly demands a federal superintendence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal control over commerce is necessary to form uniform treaties, avoid interstate commercial conflicts, prevent foreign powers exploiting state disunity, and preserve beneficial international arrangements. Separate state regulations produce impediments and animosities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized power to raise and manage armies (not mere requisitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of raising armies, by the most obvious construction of the articles of the Confederation, is merely a power of making requisitions upon the States for quotas of men. This practice... gave birth to a competition between the States which created a kind of auction for men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national government should have the authority to raise troops directly (avoid state-by-state quotas) to ensure economical, vigorous defense, stable enlistments, disciplined forces, and an equitable distribution of military burden; requisition-based quotas lead to high bounties, short enlistments, and disbandment crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional representation over equal state suffrage
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of equal suffrage among the States is another exceptionable part of the Confederation. Every idea of proportion and every rule of fair representation conspire to condemn a principle, which gives to Rhode Island an equal weight with Massachusetts, or Delaware an equal voice with Pennsylvania.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation should reflect the people's majority rather than treating sovereign States as numerically equal; equal state suffrage can result in a minority of the people (via small states) controlling the Union, provoking larger states to revolt and undermining justice and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive supermajority / unanimity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To give a minority a negative upon the majority... is, in its tendency, to subject the sense of the greater number to that of the lesser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring large majorities (or unanimity) for important decisions impedes action, invites delays, intrigue, foreign corruption (easier to bribe fewer persons), and may substitute the views of a turbulent or corrupt minority for those of a respectable majority. Simple or ordinary majorities should decide many national matters to preserve effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce vulnerability to foreign corruption by sensible decision rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When the concurrence of a large number is required by the Constitution... we forget how much good may be prevented... by the power of hindering the doing what may be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional arrangements should minimize avenues by which foreign powers can influence or bribe national decision-making (e.g., by avoiding small decisive quorums and excessive supermajority requirements); stronger, broader decision rules make external corruption harder and preserve national independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a federal judiciary / supreme tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: A circumstance which crowns the defects of the Confederation remains yet to be mentioned, the want of a judiciary power. Laws are a dead letter without courts to expound and define their true meaning and operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treaties and national laws need uniform interpretation and final adjudication; a single supreme tribunal, instituted under the authority that makes the treaties and laws, is indispensable to avoid divergent state courts producing conflicting final determinations and legal uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of law and lawful magistracy over brute force
rubrics_metrics.description: A sovereignty over sovereigns, a government over governments... in practice is subversive of the order and ends of civil polity, by substituting VIOLENCE in place of LAW, or the destructive COERCION of the SWORD in place of the mild and salutary COERCION of the MAGISTRACY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The constitution should avoid creating a structure that depends on brute force or extra-constitutional coercion; lawful magistracy and legal constitutional mechanisms are the legitimate means of enforcing union and preventing tyranny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for a federal executive to mediate and administer
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive magistrate of the union (in the Netherlands example) has authority to settle disputes between the provinces... commands the federal troops... appoints officers... presides in tribunals...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical practice shows a centralized executive (or equivalent federal authority) can prevent anarchy, settle disputes, manage foreign relations and military affairs, and fill gaps where collective bodies are ineffective; constitutional design should provide responsible executive functions without creating arbitrary monarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism to unite public councils for reform
rubrics_metrics.description: The true patriots... have made no less than four regular experiments by EXTRAORDINARY ASSEMBLIES... to apply a remedy. As many times has their laudable zeal found it impossible to UNITE THE PUBLIC COUNCILS in reforming the known... evils of the existing constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional frameworks should include practicable procedures to convene and coordinate representative bodies for constitutional or systemic reform; mere ad hoc extraordinary assemblies without effective means to unite constituent authorities are likely to fail.
